classification.difficultyReason: Construct an unsupplied proof chain: transfer side equality through the parallelogram, obtain a 60-degree exterior angle, recognise an isosceles triangle and establish that all its angles are 60 degrees.

content.prompt: The diagram shows a parallelogram $ABCD$. Prove that $\triangle BCE$ is equilateral.

spec.description: Parallelogram ABCD with horizontal AB and DC; DC extends through C to E. BE completes triangle BCE. Matching double ticks mark AD and BE. Angle DAB is labelled 120 degrees. All five vertex labels are retained, with no parallel arrows or shading.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to DC and AD is parallel to BC. D, C and E are collinear in that order. AD equals BE. The interior angle DAB is 120 degrees. Coordinates preserve the source topology and proportions and are not additional student givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no proof results or solution annotations appear.

answer.short: $BC=AD=BE$ and $\angle BCE=60^{\circ}$. Hence $\angle BEC=\angle CBE=60^{\circ}$, so $\triangle BCE$ is equilateral.
answer.worked:
$$\angle BCD=\angle DAB=120^{\circ}$$
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.

$$\angle BCE=180^{\circ}-120^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.

$$BC=AD$$
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.

The diagram marks $AD=BE$, so $BC=AD=BE$ and $\triangle BCE$ is isosceles.

$$\angle BEC=\angle BCE=60^{\circ}$$
Angles opposite equal sides of an isosceles triangle are equal.

$$\angle CBE=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$$
The angles of a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.

Therefore $\triangle BCE$ is equilateral, since all three angles are $60^{\circ}$.
